To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

proactive parenting, child RTC temperament, and parents worries about their childrens behavior are related to mothers reports of monitoring their childrens activities and companions across childhood and adolescence, and that the rate of decline in mothers monitoring reports over time is related to mothers reports about their childrens behaviors and their efforts to change those behaviors.

(a) proactive parenting, RTC temperament, and parents’ worries about their children’s behavior are associated with the level of monitoring mothers report for their children, (b) monitoring declines across time, (c) monitoring declines at a slower rate for mothers of children with RTC temperaments, and (d) monitoring declines at faster rates for mothers who report being less successful in changing their children’s behavior.

mothers who were more proactive in their parenting of their preschool-age children and who had children who were less resistant-to-control (i.e., less negative) in temperament reported more monitoring of their children's whereabouts across middle childhood and adolescence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the developmental course of mothers' monitoring of their children across childhood and adolescence.
the development and maintenance of parenting practices, and in particular the development of parental monitoring of adolescents' activities and companions.
the developmental course of mothers' reports of their monitoring across Grades 5 to 11 and with the factors that are associated with change in this domain of parenting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study provides evidence that the developmental course of monitoring across childhood and early adolescence is influenced by proactive parenting and child temperament, but not by parental worries.
proactive parenting and RTC child temperament were related to mothers' monitoring of children's activities and social contacts.
proactive parenting, child RTC temperament, and parents’ worries are associated with change in mothers' reports of monitoring across childhood and early adolescence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

proactive parenting and low resistant-to-control (RTD) child temperament were associated with higher levels of mother-reported monitoring over time, and that mothers' reports of their children's behavior and the mounting of successful behavior-change campaigns predicted a slower rate of decline in mothers' monitoring over time.
proactive parenting, child characteristics, and parents' own concerns about their children are associated with mothers' monitoring behaviors across time, with some evidence for change over time.
proactive parenting and RTC child temperament are associated with mothers' monitoring behaviors across childhood and adolescence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mothers' reports of monitoring change across development in systematic ways.
the development of mother-reported monitoring of children is associated with proactive parenting and child temperament.
mothers' monitoring of their children's daily activities is a dynamic, changing process.
